communityVoices.quote: The jam barely a minute and a half and it moves at a glacial pace. Yet you can feel the raw energy boiling under the surface waiting to explode.

communityVoices.quote: St. of Circumstance is without doubt the best I ever heard live or on tape. The stadium was comin off the chain during this.
I turned to my girlfriend and asked her what they were gonna open with...She says "Eyes of the World." I laughed and told her how they NEVER open with Eyes....And then bam.

There were massive thunderstorms right before the show. It absolutely poured. I remember people running around on the floor (or field) and sliding on the huge blue tarp they used to protect the grass like the whole place was a giant slip and slide.

whyThisShow: This is a officially released show — out as Saint of Circumstance: Giants Stadium 6/17/91 — and the community endorsement runs deep across 60 reviews. The organizing principle is a Dark Star that never quite arrives: one reviewer called it "the most Dark Star-influenced show I've ever heard, but the song proper is never played". The theme surfaces as teases and riffs throughout both sets, keeping tension coiled from the Eyes of the World opener through the second set. Multiple attendees cite this as among their best-ever Dead shows, and the SBD recording puts Bob Weir prominently forward in the mix, which matters here — one reviewer argues this was "one of Bob's best nights of the 90's". Bruce Hornsby's contributions are also central: one listener noted Hornsby "sneaks the familiar Dark Star riff into several of the songs — when's the last time you heard a DS tease in the middle of Masterpiece?".
listenFor: The Dark Star tease preceding Masterpiece in Set 1 is a specific target: one reviewer described it as "barely a minute and a half" that "moves at a glacial pace" yet with "raw energy boiling under the surface waiting to explode". The Loose Lucy drew particular attention — one attendee called it "likely the best I ever heard out of 100 shows". Saint of Circumstance was singled out as the peak of the second set, with one reviewer saying the stadium was "comin off the chain" during it. For Weir specifically, one listener recommended: "If you love Bob's work than put this show in and turn it up. He is very forward in the mix".
context: June 17, 1991 falls in the final-years era, part of a two-night Giants Stadium run — the night before also featured Dark Star teasing, and one reviewer noted the teases "incidentally they began the night before". The lineup included Bruce Hornsby on keys alongside Vince Welnick. The best-circulating recording is a soundboard (identifier: gd91-06-17.sbd.gardner.3591.sbeok.shnf). The show was officially released by the band's organization as Saint of Circumstance: Giants Stadium 6/17/91.
funFact: One reviewer recalled a Spike Lee Levi's commercial filmed at this show, noting "I remember seeing a Spike Lee commercial he did for Levi's that was filmed at this show".
headline: Eyes opener, Dark Star ghost, Giants Stadium '91.
